title: THE END OF THE BOOK, THE FAITHFULNESS OF GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"These are the commands the LORD gave Moses at Mount Sinai for the
Israelites." - Lev 27:34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
So the book of Leviticus comes to its close. One quiet sentence: these are
the commands the Lord gave. From the first chapter's offerings to this
final chapter's vows, it has all come from God, spoken at Mount Sinai to
His people.

Leviticus has not been an easy book. It is full of blood and sacrifice,
holiness and warning, careful laws and sober judgments. But step back and
look at the whole, and one great theme rises above all the details: a holy
God has made a way to dwell among an unholy people.

Dear friend, every sacrifice in this book whispered that sin is costly and
that atonement is needed. Every regulation about cleanness taught that God
is holy and cannot be approached casually. And every provision for
redemption hinted at a mercy greater than the law itself could provide.

All of it was pointing forward. Hebrews tells us that the law was only a
shadow of the good things that were coming — not the realities themselves
(Heb 10:1). The true and final sacrifice was still to come. The blood of
bulls and goats could never take away sins (Heb 10:4), but Christ, by one
sacrifice, has made perfect forever those who are being made holy (Heb
10:14).

Leviticus ends, but the story does not. Every altar in this book pointed
to a hill outside Jerusalem, where the Lamb of God would take away the sin
of the world. Read Leviticus, and let it lead you to Jesus.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has the book of Leviticus taught me about God's holiness?
2. How do the sacrifices help me appreciate the cross of Christ more?
3. Have I come to the true and final sacrifice, Jesus, for my atonement?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that every shadow in Leviticus pointed to the reality of
Christ. Thank You that a holy God has made a way to dwell with me through
the Lamb who takes away my sin. Amen.
